Innermost-parent first, // root last. An empty string represents the document root (no // iteration); the tree widget renders the raw source shape for it. // A records-path with 0 `[*]` produces nothing. // // Example: `{{[*].subgroups[*].items[*]}}` → // `{{[*].subgroups[*]}}` (innermost parent — subgroups) // `{{[*]}}` (outer ancestor — top-level groups) // `` (root document) // // Used by the path-pick modal to render one tree per ancestor scope. // The modal's depth counter (1, 2, …, nStars) matches the number of // `../` segments needed to reach each scope from the innermost record. const extractToken = (recordsPath) => { let path = null walkTemplate(recordsPath, () => {}, () => {}, (content) => { if (path === null) path = parseToken(content).path } ) return path === null ? recordsPath : path } exports['jc-records-parent-paths'] = function(source) { const out = [] source((tiddler, title) => { const tokenPath = extractToken(title) const segments = parsePath(tokenPath) if (!segments) return const stars = [] for (let i = 0; i < segments.length; i++) { if (segments[i].type === 'star') stars.push(i) } const nStars = stars.length if (nStars === 0) return for (let depth = 1; depth < nStars; depth++) { const idx = nStars - depth - 1 const parentSegs = segments.slice(0, stars[idx] + 1) out.push(`{{${renderPathSegments(parentSegs)}}}`) } out.push('') }) return out } // For an input records-path and a depth (1 = innermost-parent, …, // nStars = root), return the key segment that bridges into the // next-deeper scope — i.e. the key the picker should HIDE at this // ancestor's tree so users don't see noise like the `activities` // entry inside the `days[*]` scope. Returns empty if the bridging // segment isn't a plain key (e.g. adjacent `[*]`s or bare-array root). // // Example: `{{days[*].activities[*]}}` with depth=1 → `activities`, // depth=2 → `days`. `{{[*].subgroups[*]}}` depth=2 → `` (bare array). exports['jc-records-hide-key'] = function(source, operator) { const depth = Number.parseInt(operator.operand, 10) const out = [] source((_, title) => { const segments = parsePath(extractToken(title)) if (!segments || Number.isNaN(depth) || depth < 1) { out.push('') return } const stars = [] for (let i = 0; i < segments.length; i++) { if (segments[i].type === 'star') stars.push(i) } const nStars = stars.length if (depth > nStars) { out.push('') return } const idx = depth === nStars ? 0 : stars[nStars - 1 - depth] + 1 const seg = segments[idx] out.push(seg && seg.type === 'key' ? seg.key : '') }) return out } // Strip the `{{` / `}}` wrapping from a records-path template, so the // inner path can be shown in a heading. Exists because TW's attribute // parser treats `"{{"` as an empty transclusion, making the natural // `trimprefix[{{]trimsuffix[}}]` approach unusable both directly and // via indirect operand. exports['jc-strip-template-braces'] = function(source) { const out = [] source((_, title) => { if (title.length >= 4 && title.startsWith('{{') && title.endsWith('}}')) { out.push(title.slice(2, -2)) } else { out.push(title) } }) return out } ","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"filteroperator"},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/filters/repeat-string.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/filters/repeat-string.js","text":"// For each input title parsed as a non-negative integer N, emit the // operator's operand string repeated N times. Used by the path-pick // modal to build `../` prefixes from a depth count. // // Example: `[[3]jc-repeat-string[../]]` → `../../../` exports['jc-repeat-string'] = function(source, operator) { const out = [] const str = operator.operand || '' source((tiddler, title) => { const n = Number.parseInt(title, 10) if (Number.isNaN(n) || n < 0) return out.push(str.repeat(n)) }) return out } '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/engine/transforms.js' ) const { walkTemplate, parseToken, parseTransform } = require( '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/engine/template.js' ) const { prepareSource } = require( '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/engine/prepare.js' ) const { resolvePath } = require( '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/engine/path.js' ) const { mergeRecordShapes } = require( '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/engine/shape.js' ) const { serializeShape, topLevelFields } = require( '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/engine/shape-diff.js' ) const { extractRecordsToken } = require( '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/widgets/util.js' ) // Pure construction of an importer pack — the plugin tiddler a // recipient installs — from a profile, the transforms it references, // optional sample data, and the form the author filled in. No wiki // access: the widget gathers the inputs, this module builds the // output, and the tests exercise it headlessly. const RUNTIME_TITLE = '$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert' const PROFILE_TAG = '$:/tags/json-convert/profile' const TRANSFORM_TAG = '$:/tags/json-convert/transform' const PROFILE_FORMAT = 1 const TYPE_JS = 'application/javascript' const SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ const VERSION_RE = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/ const COLLISIONS = new Set(['skip', 'overwrite']) const isPlainObject = (v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) const err = (code, message) => ({ code, message }) const compareVersions = (a, b) => { const pa = a.split('.').map(Number) const pb = b.split('.').map(Number) for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { if (pa[i] !== pb[i]) return pa[i] > pb[i] ? 1 : -1 } return 0 } const bumpPatch = (version) => { const [major, minor, patch] = version.split('.').map(Number) return `${major}.${minor}.${patch + 1}` } const packTitleFor = (publisher, slug) => `$:/plugins/${publisher}/${slug}` // Every transform name a profile's bindings pipe through. const referencedTransforms = (profile) => { const names = new Set() const scan = (template) => { if (typeof template !== 'string') return walkTemplate(template, () => {}, () => {}, (content) => { parseToken(content).transforms.forEach((spec) => { const { name } = parseTransform(spec) if (name) names.add(name) }) }) } for (const group of ['tw-fields', 'custom-fields']) { const bindings = profile[group] if (isPlainObject(bindings)) Object.values(bindings).forEach(scan) } return names } // The shape of the sample's records, recorded so the consumer panel can // later compare what a recipient pastes against what the profile was // built for. Null when the sample cannot be read the way the profile // reads it — the author sees that as a generation error instead. const fingerprint = (sampleText, profile) => { const prepared = prepareSource(sampleText, profile.normalize) if (prepared.errors.length) { return { error: prepared.errors[0].message } } const records = resolvePath( prepared.value, extractRecordsToken(profile.records) ) if (!Array.isArray(records) || records.length === 0) { return { error: `records path ${profile.records} matches nothing in the sample` } } return { records: profile.records, count: records.length, shape: serializeShape(mergeRecordShapes(records)) } } const runtimeLink = (studioUrl) => `${studioUrl}#${encodeURIComponent(RUNTIME_TITLE)}` const shimText = ({ runtimeMin, studioUrl, panelTitle }) => { const where = studioUrl ? `Drag [[the ${RUNTIME_TITLE} tiddler|${runtimeLink(studioUrl)}]] into this wiki, save, and reload.` : `Ask whoever gave you this importer for the \`${RUNTIME_TITLE}\` plugin; drag it into this wiki, save, and reload.` return [ `<$let panel="${RUNTIME_TITLE}/ui/consumer-panel">`, `<$list filter="[is[tiddler]] [is[shadow]] +[first[]]" variable="_jc" emptyMessage="""`, `This importer needs the ''JSON Convert'' runtime plugin (version ${runtimeMin} or newer), which is not installed in this wiki. ${where}`, `""">`, '<$transclude', ' $tiddler=<>', ' $mode="block"', ` pack="${panelTitle}"/>`, '', '', '' ].join('\n') } const readmeText = ({ name, description, caption, panelTitle, studioUrl, runtimeMin, version, now, fields }) => { const date = `${now.slice(0, 4)}-${now.slice(4, 6)}-${now.slice(6, 8)}` const made = studioUrl ? `[[JSON Convert Studio|${studioUrl}]]` : 'JSON Convert Studio' const lines = [ `! ${name}`, '', description, '', `* [[${caption}|${panelTitle}]] — open the importer. It is also listed under ''More › Importers'' in the sidebar.` ] if (fields.length) { lines.push(`* It expects JSON records with the fields ${fields.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(', ')}.`) } lines.push( `* How to use it: [[Using an importer|${RUNTIME_TITLE}/usage]].`, `* Version ${version}, made ${date} with ${made}. Needs the JSON Convert runtime ${runtimeMin} or newer. If your JSON stops fitting, ask whoever made this importer for a regenerated copy.`, '' ) return lines.join('\n') } const validateForm = (form) => { const errors = [] if (!SLUG_RE.test(form.publisher || '')) { errors.push(err('bad-publisher', 'publisher must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "acme"')) } if (!SLUG_RE.test(form.slug || '')) { errors.push(err('bad-slug', 'slug must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "invoice-importer"')) } if (!(form.name || '').trim()) { errors.push(err('missing-name', 'the importer needs a name')) } if (!(form.caption || '').trim()) { errors.push(err('missing-caption', 'the importer page needs a caption')) } if (!VERSION_RE.test(form.version || '')) { errors.push(err('bad-version', 'version must look like 1.2.3')) } if (form.collisions && !COLLISIONS.has(form.collisions)) { errors.push(err('bad-collisions', 'the collision default must be "skip" or "overwrite"')) } return errors } // input: // form — { profile, publisher, slug, name, description, author, // version, caption, panelDescription, convertLabel, // applyLabel, collisions, studioUrl } // profile — { title, text, fields } (the source profile) // transforms — { [name]: { title, fields, builtin } } (every user // transform in the wiki; builtin ones ship with the // runtime and are never copied) // sample — { title, text } or null // runtime — { title, version, coreVersion } // installed — version string of a pack already at the target title, // or null // now — TiddlyWiki date string for created/modified const buildPack = (input) => { const { form, profile, transforms, sample, runtime, installed, now } = input const errors = validateForm(form) let parsed = null if (!profile) { errors.push(err('missing-profile', 'no profile selected')) } else { try { parsed = JSON.parse(profile.text || '') } catch (e) { errors.push(err('profile-not-json', `profile "${profile.title}" is not valid JSON: ${e.message}`)) } } const available = {} for (const name of Object.keys(transforms || {})) available[name] = true if (parsed !== null) { validateProfile(parsed, available).forEach((e) => { errors.push(err('profile-invalid', `${e.code}: ${e.message}`)) }) } if (installed && form.version && VERSION_RE.test(form.version) && compareVersions(form.version, installed) <= 0) { errors.push(err('version-not-newer', `version ${installed} of this importer is already installed here; ` + `use ${bumpPatch(installed)} or higher so the new one replaces it`)) } let shape = null if (parsed !== null && errors.length === 0 && sample) { shape = fingerprint(sample.text || '', parsed) if (shape.error) { errors.push(err('sample-mismatch', `the sample does not fit the profile: ${shape.error}`)) } } if (errors.length) return { errors } const packTitle = packTitleFor(form.publisher, form.slug) const t = (rest) => `${packTitle}/${rest}` const tiddlers = {} const copied = [] let containsJs = false for (const name of referencedTransforms(parsed)) { if (defaultTransforms[name]) continue const entry = transforms[name] if (!entry || entry.builtin) continue const title = t(`transforms/${name}`) tiddlers[title] = { ...entry.fields, title, name, tags: TRANSFORM_TAG } copied.push(name) if (entry.fields.type === TYPE_JS) containsJs = true } const profileTitle = t('profile') tiddlers[profileTitle] = { title: profileTitle, caption: form.name.trim(), tags: PROFILE_TAG, type: 'application/json', text: formatProfile({ format: PROFILE_FORMAT, ...parsed }) } let sampleTitle = '' if (sample) { sampleTitle = t('sample') tiddlers[sampleTitle] = { title: sampleTitle, type: 'application/json', text: sample.text } const shapeTitle = t('shape') tiddlers[shapeTitle] = { title: shapeTitle, type: 'application/json', text: JSON.stringify(shape) } } const panelTitle = t('importer') const panel = { title: panelTitle, caption: form.caption.trim(), type: 'text/vnd.tiddlywiki', slug: form.slug, profile: profileTitle, 'convert-label': (form.convertLabel || '').trim() || 'Convert', 'apply-label': (form.applyLabel || '').trim() || 'Apply', collisions: form.collisions || 'skip', 'runtime-min': runtime.version, text: shimText({ runtimeMin: runtime.version, studioUrl: form.studioUrl, panelTitle }) } if (sampleTitle) { panel.sample = sampleTitle panel.shape = t('shape') } if ((form.author || '').trim()) panel.author = form.author.trim() if (form.studioUrl) panel['studio-url'] = form.studioUrl if ((form.panelDescription || '').trim()) { panel.description = form.panelDescription.trim() } tiddlers[panelTitle] = panel const description = (form.description || '').trim() || `Imports ${form.name.trim()} JSON as tiddlers` const readmeTitle = t('readme') tiddlers[readmeTitle] = { title: readmeTitle, type: 'text/vnd.tiddlywiki', text: readmeText({ name: form.name.trim(), description, caption: form.caption.trim(), panelTitle, studioUrl: form.studioUrl, runtimeMin: runtime.version, version: form.version, now, fields: shape ? topLevelFields(shape.shape) : [] }) } const pack = { title: packTitle, name: form.name.trim(), description, author: (form.author || '').trim(), version: guide","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"! Understanding profiles A //profile// is a small JSON document that tells JSON Convert how to turn your source JSON into TiddlyWiki tiddlers. It does two things, and only two things: * Picks which parts of the source become individual tiddlers (the ''records''). * Describes, for each record, what the resulting tiddler's fields should look like (the ''bindings''). That's the whole concept. The rest of this guide is detail. This is the canonical reference for profiles. If you want a faster start, the [[Console|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/Console]] ships with sample profiles you can open in the editor and learn from. When you want depth — what `..` means in a binding, why your custom transform isn't showing in the picker, what `binding-token-star` means — come back here. ''Contents'' * §1 What a profile looks like * §2 Anatomy: `records`, `tw-fields`, `custom-fields` * §3 Bindings * §4 Path expressions * §5 Transforms * §6 Writing a profile by hand * §7 Building one with the editor * §8 Where to go next --- ! 1. What a profile looks like Here is a complete profile for a flat list of books. Source JSON: ``` { "books": [ { "title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert", "year": 1965 }, { "title": "Neuromancer", "author": "William Gibson", "year": 1984 }, { "title": "Kindred", "author": "Octavia Butler", "year": 1979 } ] } ``` The profile: ``` { "records": "{{books[*]}}", "tw-fields": { "title": "{{author}}: {{title}}", "tags": "Book" }, "custom-fields": { "year": "{{year}}" } } ``` After Convert + Apply you get three tiddlers: |!Title |!`tags` |!`year` | |Frank Herbert: Dune |Book |1965 | |William Gibson: Neuromancer |Book |1984 | |Octavia Butler: Kindred |Book |1979 | Each block is doing one thing: * `records` says //iterate `books[*]`, one tiddler per element//. * `tw-fields` populates the tiddler's built-in fields. `{{author}}` and `{{title}}` are //tokens// — they look up the named path in the current record. * `custom-fields` does the same for any other field you want on the resulting tiddler. That's the whole vocabulary. The next sections take each piece apart. --- ! 2. Anatomy A profile is a JSON object with up to three top-level keys, in any order: |!Key |!What it does | |`records` |A template identifying the source array to iterate | |`tw-fields` |Bindings for built-in tiddler fields (`title`, `tags`, …) | |`custom-fields` |Bindings for every other field on the resulting tiddler | `records` is mandatory. `tw-fields` and `custom-fields` are both optional, but at least one of them must contain a `title` binding so each resulting tiddler has a title. In practice you'll always have `title` under `tw-fields`. !! 2.1 `records` `records` is a //template// containing exactly one path token wrapped in `{{ … }}`: ``` "records": "{{books[*]}}" ``` The path inside must resolve to an array. The `[*]` operator says //for every element of that array, emit one record//. See §4.3 for the full path grammar. A profile produces one tiddler per record element — three books above, twelve activities for a three-day Iceland trip, however many your source has. `records` can walk through multiple `[*]`s in one path: `{{days[*].activities[*]}}` produces one record per activity across all days. See §4.4. !! 2.2 `tw-fields` The built-in TiddlyWiki fields go here. Conventionally that means `title`, `tags`, `text`, `type`, `created`, `modified`, `creator`, `modifier`. Each maps to a binding (§3) producing the value written to that field on each resulting tiddler. Typical bindings: * `"title": "{{author}}: {{title}}"` — a title built from two source fields. * `"tags": "Book {{genre|split-commas}}"` — a static word plus a list-formatted source value. * `"created": "{{created_at|iso-to-date}}"` — an ISO timestamp converted to TiddlyWiki's `YYYYMMDDhhmmssXXX` format. You don't have to bind every built-in field. Anything you skip is left unset on the resulting tiddler (TW will fill in `created` and `modified` automatically if you don't). !! 2.3 `custom-fields` Everything else — domain-specific fields you want on the resulting tiddler — goes here. Same binding syntax, same path expressions, same transforms. The only practical difference from `tw-fields` is that the field name isn't constrained by TiddlyWiki convention; pick whatever fits your data. ``` "custom-fields": { "year": "{{year}}", "publisher": "{{publisher.name}}", "isbn-13": "{{isbn}}" } ``` The validator catches collisions between `tw-fields` and `custom-fields` (error code `field-redefined`) so the same field name can't appear in both blocks. --- ! 3. Bindings A //binding// is a string template. Most bindings are short — one token, sometimes a token plus literal text. Examples already appeared above; this section names the parts. !! 3.1 Plain text A binding with no `{{ … }}` is used verbatim: ``` "tags": "Book" ``` Every resulting tiddler gets the literal string `Book` as its `tags`. !! 3.2 `{{path}}` tokens `{{path}}` substitutes the value at `path` (resolved against the current record) into the binding. Numbers, booleans, and null auto-stringify; arrays and objects become their JSON serialisations. ``` "title": "{{title}}" "caption": "{{author}}" ``` !! 3.3 Mixing tokens and text A binding can interleave any number of tokens with surrounding text: ``` "title": "{{author}}: {{title}} ({{year}})" ``` For the first book above this produces `Frank Herbert: Dune (1965)`. Single `{` or `}` characters in a binding are literal — you only need the double form when you want a token. !! 3.4 Missing paths If a token's path doesn't resolve (the field is missing on this particular record), the token expands to an empty string. No error. This makes profiles tolerant of irregular input: some records may have a field that others don't, and you don't have to special-case each one. If you //want// to be strict, eyeball the staging area before Apply — it shows the resolved values for every tiddler about to be written. --- ! 4. Path expressions A //path expression// is what goes inside `{{ … }}`. It walks the source JSON. Most paths are short; the syntax scales to handle arbitrary nesting when you need it. !! 4.1 Keys and dots Dot-separate object keys: ``` {{publisher.name}} {{address.country.code}} ``` Keys can contain anything that isn't `.`, `[`, `]`, or `/`. !! 4.2 Array indices Numeric brackets pick a specific element: ``` {{authors[0]}} {{tags[2]}} ``` Useful when the source structure is fixed (position 0 is always the primary author, etc.). !! 4.3 `[*]` — iteration The star says //iterate every element//. In `records` (§2.1), `[*]` defines what becomes a tiddler. In a //binding// token, `[*]` is not allowed (validator error `binding-token-star`) — bindings must resolve to a single value per record, and `[*]` produces many. If you want to flatten an array into a binding (e.g. a list of tags), the `split-commas` transform (§5) formats an array as a wikitext list. !! 4.4 Nested iteration `records` can use multiple `[*]`s to flatten nested arrays. Given: ``` { "days": [ { "date": "2023-09-01", "activities": [...] }, { "date": "2023-09-02", "activities": [...] } ] } ``` a profile with `"records": "{{days[*].activities[*]}}"` produces one tiddler per activity across all days. Three days × four activities each = twelve tiddlers. !! 4.5 Ancestor scopes — `..` Once a profile iterates `days[*].activities[*]`, the "current record" is an activity object. Activity-level fields are reachable as `{{name}}`, `{{duration}}`, etc. But what about the day's `date` or the trip's `country`? Those live one or two levels //above// the current record. The `..` segment walks up one iteration scope: |!Token |!Reaches | |`{{name}}` |the current activity's name | |`{{../date}}` |the day's date (one up) | |`{{../../trip-name}}` |the trip name (two up, root) | Stack as many `..` as you have `[*]`s in `records`. More than that is an error (`binding-parent-too-deep`). !! 4.6 Bare-array roots Sometimes the source isn't an object but a top-level array: ``` [ { "id": 1, "name": "Alice" }, { "id": 2, "name": "Bob" } ] ``` The records path can start with `[*]`: ``` "records": "{{[*]}}" ``` Combined with nested iteration: `"records": "{{[*].pages[*]}}"`. --- ! 5. Transforms A //transform// is a named function that reshapes a token's value before substitution. Pipe a transform onto a token with `|`: |!Token |!Effect | |`{{title\|to-upper-case}}` |`"Dune"` → `"DUNE"` | |`{{genre\|split-commas}}` |`"sci-fi, classic"` → `"sci-fi classic"` | |`{{created_at\|iso-to-date}}` |`"2026-05-17T21:36:24Z"` → `"20260517213624000"` | !! 5.1 Chaining Multiple transforms run left-to-right: ``` {{title|to-lower-case|slugify}} ``` The output of `to-lower-case` becomes the input to `slugify`. No arbitrary limit on chain length. !! 5.2 Plugin-shipped transforms |!Name |!Input → Output | |`html-to-wikitext` |Placeholder for upcoming HTML conversion; currently pass-through | |`split-commas` |`"a, b, c"` (or array) → `"a b c"`, `[[ ]]`-quoting any item with whitespace | |`timestamp-to-date` |Numeric epoch (seconds or ms) → TW `YYYYMMDDhhmmssXXX` UTC | |`iso-to-date` |ISO 8601 string → TW `YYYYMMDDhhmmssXXX` UTC | |`to-upper-case` |`"hello"` → `"HELLO"` | |`to-lower-case` |`"HELLO"` → `"hello"` | |`to-title-case` |`"hello world"` → `"Hello World"` | |`slugify` |`"Hello, World!"` → `"hello-world"` | |`zero-pad[width]` |`7` → `"007"` with `zero-pad[3]` | |`default[text]` |an empty or missing value → `text` | |`prefix[text]`, `suffix[text]` |`42` → `"#42"`, `"42%"` | |`replace[from],[to]` |every occurrence of `from` → `to` | |`pluck[key]` |`[{"name":"a"},{"name":"b"}]` → `"a b"` | Parameters go in brackets after the name, comma-separated when there are several — the same shape as a filter operand. Three //context paths// stand in for a field: `{{@now}}` (the import time), `{{@counter}}` (the record's number, from 1) and `{{@record}}` (the whole record as JSON). !! 5.3 User-defined transforms Add your own by creating a tiddler tagged `$:/tags/json-convert/transform`. JavaScript bodies expose `value` (the input string) and return the transformed string; wikitext bodies run as filter expressions with `value` in scope. See the [[Usage guide|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage]] §8 for full details and worked examples. The transform's name is its tiddler title (or `caption`, if set). Names appear in the editor's Browse-modal transform picker alongside the built-ins. --- ! 6. Writing a profile by hand You don't have to use the editor. A profile is just a JSON tiddler tagged `$:/tags/json-convert/profile`. !! 6.1 The minimum ``` title: My First Profile tags: $:/tags/json-convert/profile type: application/json { "records": "{{[*]}}", "tw-fields": { "title": "{{name}}" } } ``` Drag the source JSON into the Console, pick ''My First Profile'' from the profile dropdown, Convert, Apply. !! 6.2 Naming Use any human-readable title — `Example Trip Itinerary`, `Moodle Quiz`, `Bookshelf Import`. No `$:/` namespace required. The plugin watches the tag, not the title. !! 6.3 Common gotchas * ''Token vs. literal''. `{{author}}` is a token; `{author}` is the literal text `{author}` — no substitution. Double braces are required. * ''Quoting JSON''. `records` is a JSON string, so the binding inside is `"{{books[*]}}"` (the outer quotes belong to JSON; the inner braces belong to the binding language). * ''Field collisions''. If a key appears in both `tw-fields` and `custom-fields`, the validator reports `field-redefined`. Pick one block. * ''Trailing commas''. JSON doesn't allow them. The validator will surface a `bad-shape` error. * ''Forgetting to tag''. An untagged profile won't appear in the Console's dropdown. The tag is `$:/tags/json-convert/profile`. !! 6.4 Validating The fastest validation loop is to open your hand-written profile in the editor (Console → select profile → ''Edit''). The editor runs the validator live and shows every error in-line with click-to-scroll links. Errors that aren't editor-resolvable (e.g. a typo in the JSON itself) show the raw error code from the [[Usage guide|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage]] §10.4. --- ! 7. Building a profile with the editor The editor is the recommended way to build and tweak profiles. It handles the JSON serialisation, runs live validation, and offers point-and-click pickers backed by the actual source JSON. ''Screenshot needed:'' the Editor open on a sample profile, with the records path field at top, the source JSON pane on the right, and the `tw-fields` / `custom-fields` tables in the middle. !! 7.1 Opening the editor From the Console: * ''New…'' opens an empty editor. Pick the source JSON, name the profile, start binding. * ''Edit'' opens the currently-selected profile. Edits save live as you type (debounced ~200ms); see §7.8. !! 7.2 The Sample JSON pane The right-hand pane shows the source JSON the editor is using as its //example// — what every path is resolved against in the live preview. The Console and the editor //share// this state, so whatever's in the Console source area is also what the editor uses for path resolution. If you don't have a source ready, paste any small example. All the pickers (records, paths, fields) walk this JSON to suggest names. !! 7.3 Picking the records path Above the fields tables is a single ''records'' field with a ''Browse'' button. Click Browse and a modal opens showing the source JSON as a tree. ''Screenshot needed:'' the ''Pick the records path'' modal — the JSON-shape tree with one of the arrays highlighted, ready for selection. Click ''copy'' on the array you want to iterate. If you click on a specific element (e.g. `[0]`), the picker rewrites that to `[*]` automatically so the records path matches all siblings, not just the one you happened to click on. !! 7.4 Adding `tw-fields` bindings Below the records field are two tables: ''tw-fields'' and ''custom-fields''. Each row is a single binding. To add a row, type the field name (`title`, `tags`, etc.) and click ''Add''; then click the new row's ''Browse'' button to fill the binding template. ''Screenshot needed:'' the `tw-fields` table mid-edit, with a few rows filled in, cursor in the title row, and the Browse modal open showing ''Current record'' tree plus an ''Ancestor: `../`'' tree. The path modal shows one tree per scope: * ''Current record'' — the shape of the iteration target. Pick fields here for tokens like `{{name}}`. * ''Ancestor: `../`'' (and `../../`, etc. for deeper records paths) — fields one or more scopes up. Picking from these scopes inserts the appropriate `../` prefix automatically. Each click on a tree row's ''copy'' button inserts a `{{path}}` token at the cursor position in the binding input. Type literal text between tokens for compound bindings like `"{{author}}: {{title}}"`. !! 7.5 Adding `custom-fields` bindings Same workflow, different table. Custom field names are user-defined; the editor accepts anything that doesn't collide with a `tw-fields` row. !! 7.6 The Browse modal in binding mode The modal's ''Optional transform'' dropdown attaches a transform to every path you pick from this modal session. Useful when you're binding several date fields in a row and want `|iso-to-date` on all of them: pick the transform once, then click your way through the source. You can always edit the binding manually after picking — chain more transforms, add literal text, whatever. !! 7.7 The pass-through field picker When the source has dozens of fields and you want most of them as custom-fields with their JSON keys as field names, the ''Custom Fields'' header has a ''Pick fields…'' button. It opens a checkbox tree of every leaf in the source. ''Screenshot needed:'' the ''Pick fields'' modal open on the Moodle Gradebook sample, showing the checkbox tree with editable field-name inputs to the right of the checkboxes. Tick the leaves you want; they land as custom-fields bindings on Apply, with their JSON key auto-flattened (slugified) into a tiddler field name you can override inline. The picker supports tri-state ''All'' (header), Select-all / Clear-all bulk buttons, and inline-editable field names. !! 7.8 Live save, debounce, revert The editor saves your draft live, debounced ~200ms after the last keystroke. No ''Save'' button. When you open a profile via ''Edit'', the original is snapshotted; the editor's revert action restores the snapshot if you decide your edits weren't what you wanted. --- ! 8. Where to go next * [[Usage guide|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage]] — Console workflow, recipes, full error-code reference, plugin internals. * The sample profiles in the demo wiki — each demonstrates a different pattern (flat records, nested iteration, ancestor refs, pass-through picking, transforms). Open them in the editor to see how they're put together. * [[Changelog]] — what's new across releases.     "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/appendix-a":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/appendix-a","caption":"Appendix A — Differences from TiddlyWiki's built-in JSON importer","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"TiddlyWiki's core has an importer that handles JSON drag-and-drop, but it's designed for JSON whose shape is already //tiddler-like// — an array of objects whose keys map directly onto tiddler fields, with string values. Differences: |! |!Core importer |!JSON Convert | |Source shape |must match tiddler shape |arbitrary JSON; the profile bridges the shapes | |Non-string fields |silently dropped |coerced via automatic stringification or transforms | |Field renaming |not supported |bindings choose any target name | |Title derivation |source must have `title` field |compose from any fields via a template | |Nested-record iteration |not supported |`[*].subgroups[*].items[*]` plus `..` ancestor refs | |Custom per-field processing |none |built-in and user-defined transforms | |Conflict handling |dialog per file |per-row skip/overwrite/rename in a staging area | |Tolerant input |strict |strips BOM/junk; emits recoverable warnings | If your JSON is already tiddler-shaped, the core importer is simpler. For anything else, JSON Convert is the tool. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/appendix-b":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/appendix-b","caption":"Appendix B — Notes for plugin developers","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The engine (`engine/parser.js`, `engine/path.js`, `engine/template.js`, `engine/transforms.js`, `engine/validate.js`, `engine/convert.js`, `engine/shape.js`) is //pure JavaScript with no TiddlyWiki dependency//. It's testable in plain Node — see the project's `test/` directory. The widgets (`widgets/*.js`) and filter operators (`filters/*.js`) are the TiddlyWiki-side glue: they collect user transforms, parse the profile, call the engine, write staged tiddlers, and render the editor UI. Useful entry points: * ''`convert(jsonText, profile, existingTitles, options)`'' — engine entry point. `options.transforms` extends the built-in transform registry. * ''`validateProfile(profile, transforms)`'' — pure validator; returns an array of error objects. * ''`collectUserTransforms(wiki)`'' — TiddlyWiki-side helper that builds the transform map by scanning tagged tiddlers. No hooks are exposed today (no event before/after Apply, no per-record filter). If you have a use case for one, the architecture doc and the project's planning files in `.meta/` are good places to start a conversation. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console/apply-cancel":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console/apply-cancel","caption":"Apply / Cancel","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"''Apply'' walks the staged rows, executes each row's chosen action against the wiki, then clears the staged and decision tiddlers. The Console renders that list as clickable links under ''Imported this session''. The list resets on wiki reload — `$:/temp/...` isn't persisted. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console/source-json":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console/source-json","caption":"Source JSON","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The Source JSON area accepts input three ways: * ''Paste'' — text directly into the textarea. Works for typical sizes; for multi-megabyte JSON, use a file pick or drop instead. * ''Choose File'' — the file picker reads any `.json`/`.txt` file via `FileReader.readAsText`. * ''Drag-and-drop'' — drop a file onto the dropzone (the textarea). The plugin intercepts the drop in the capturing phase so TiddlyWiki's own drag-and-drop importer doesn't try to read the file. ''Tolerant parser.'' Before parsing, the engine strips a leading byte-order mark and trims leading/trailing non-JSON noise (anything before the first `{` or `[`, and anything after the matching close). When recovery succeeds, a ''parse-recovered'' warning appears; if it fails, you get a ''parse-failed'' error with the column position. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console/staging":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console/staging","caption":"Staging","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/console","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Each staged tiddler is a real tiddler under `$:/temp/...` carrying its intended target title in a `_target-title` field and, if the target already exists in the wiki, a `_collision: yes` marker. The staging UI splits them into two sections: * ''Conflicts'' — rows whose target title already exists. Default action: //skip//. Per-row choices: //skip//, //overwrite//, //rename//. Bulk: ''Set all to: Skip | Overwrite''. Rename is per-row only and reveals an input for the new title with live validation. * ''New'' — rows whose target title is new. Default action: //add//. Per-row choices: //add//, //skip//. Bulk: ''Set all to: Add | Skip''. Each row expands ({{$:/core/images/right-arrow}} / {{$:/core/images/down-arrow}}) to show the staged tiddler's fields and a native TiddlyWiki preview of its `text` field. The body is a //function body// (not a function expression). In scope: `value`; `params`, the bracketed parameters as an array of strings (`{{x|year-bucket[10]}}` gives `['10']`); `record`, the whole current record; and `counter`, the record's position counting from 1. Whatever you `return` becomes the transformed value: ``` title: Year Bucket name: year-bucket tags: $:/tags/json-convert/transform type: application/javascript const n = Number(value) if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return '' return String(Math.floor(n / 10) * 10) + 's' ``` A `2007` input becomes `"2000s"`. Read `params[0]` to make the bucket width a parameter, and `record.someOtherField` when the result depends on more than the one value. ''Errors.'' If the body fails to compile (`SyntaxError`), the transform is skipped entirely — using it in a profile produces ''unknown-transform''. If it throws at run time, the affected token resolves to the empty string but the conversion continues. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/naming":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/naming","caption":"Naming","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms [[Transforms Guide]]","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The transform's profile-facing name comes from the tiddler's `name` field. If `name` is absent, the title is run through the plugin's slugify rule (lowercase, runs of non-alphanumerics → `-`, trim leading/trailing dashes). So a tiddler titled `$:/plugins/me/json-convert-extras/foo Bar` becomes `plugins-me-json-convert-extras-foo-bar` — definitely set `name` explicitly unless your title is already a clean identifier. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/visibility":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/visibility","caption":"Visibility","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms [[Transforms Guide]]","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"User-defined transforms show up automatically in the Browse modal's transform picker once their tiddler is saved. If a profile names a transform that the picker does not show, the ''unknown-transform'' error says why when it can: the tiddler carrying that name has no `type` (or one that is not `application/javascript` or `text/vnd.tiddlywiki`), its JavaScript does not compile, or it has the `name` but not the `$:/tags/json-convert/transform` tag. Leaving the type unset is the usual one: a tiddler created through TiddlyWiki's own editor has no type until you pick one. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/wikitext":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/wikitext","caption":"Wikitext transforms","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms [[Transforms Guide]]","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"`type: text/vnd.tiddlywiki`. The body is wikitext rendered with these variables in scope: `value`; `param`, the first bracketed parameter; `params`, all of them as a title list; `record`, the current record as JSON text (reach into it with `jsonget`); and `counter`, the record's position counting from 1. The rendered output (as plain text) is the transformed value. Inline-filter style is the common idiom: ``` title: Slugify name: slugify tags: $:/tags/json-convert/transform type: text/vnd.tiddlywiki \define non-alnum() [^a-z0-9]+ \define edge-dashes() ^-+|-+$ {{{ [lowercase[]search-replace:g:regexp,[-]search-replace:g:regexp,[]] }}} ``` The two `\define` lines hold the regex patterns: TW's filter-operand syntax can't carry a `[...]` character class directly inside `[...]` operand brackets, so the patterns are passed through variables. But the body is //full wikitext// — anything TiddlyWiki can render is fair game: macros, `<$let>` chains, `<$list>` filters, transclusions, custom widgets installed alongside this plugin. A more involved example: ``` title: Truncate name: truncate tags: $:/tags/json-convert/transform type: text/vnd.tiddlywiki \whitespace trim <$let n={{{ [length[]] }}}> <$list filter="[compare:number:gt[40]]" emptyMessage=<>> {{{ [substr[0],[37]] }}}… ``` Strings of 40 characters or fewer pass through unchanged; longer ones are truncated to 37 characters with an ellipsis. The `\whitespace trim` pragma keeps the rendered output clean of stray whitespace. ''When to use which.'' JavaScript wins for complex algorithms, regex with lookbehinds, multi-step parsing. Wikitext wins for filter-operator chains, anything you'd already write as a TW macro, and transforms that need to reach into wiki state — a filter like `[listed[init]]` looks a value up against the tiddlers around it; see [[Looking up a related tiddler at import|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/lookup-at-import]]. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms","caption":"Writing your own transform","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/js $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/wikitext $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/visibility $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/custom-transforms/naming","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A transform is a tiddler tagged `$:/tags/json-convert/transform`. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/fields-tables":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/fields-tables","caption":"Fields tables","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Below the records path sit two tables joined visually but distinct in storage: * ''TiddlyWiki Fields'' — `title`, `tags`, `caption`, `text` plus a pill row for adding common standard fields (`author`, `color`, `created`, …) and a ''more…'' toggle for the long tail (`_canonical_uri`, `bag`, …). * ''Custom Fields'' — adds rows on demand via the ''Add'' button in the section header. Each row's //name// is editable inline. Duplicate detection (vs other custom names and vs TW field names) is live. ''Row states.'' Each row has two visual modes: * ''Display'' — name + value + transform shown as plain text, with ''Edit'' and ''×'' buttons. Validation problems flag the row with a red left edge; the inline error appears in edit mode. * ''Edit'' — name (custom rows only), value, and transform become editable; a ''Browse…'' button appears next to the value. Click ''Done'' to collapse back to display. Pills and ''Add'' open the new row directly into edit mode with the cursor ready for the value. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/live-save":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/live-save","caption":"Live save, debounce, revert","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The editor writes the profile body on every change — debounced at ~200 ms so it doesn't fire on every keystroke. No save button. When you //first// open the editor on a profile, a snapshot of the current profile is taken in `$:/temp/json-convert/editor/backup`. A yellow ''Revert to backup'' bar appears below the validation banner once the backup exists — clicking it restores the profile to its pre-edit state. The backup resets on wiki reload (it lives in `$:/temp/...`). "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/pass-through":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/pass-through","caption":"The pass-through field picker","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Beside the Custom Fields header sits a ''Pick fields…'' button. It opens a modal showing every leaf field in the source JSON's record-scoped shape, each with a checkbox and a proposed field name. Tick the fields you want; click ''Apply''. Each ticked leaf becomes a custom-fields entry of the form `"": "{{}}"` — pure pass-through, no transform. The picker is the right tool when most of the source's fields should land verbatim in the produced tiddlers and only a handful of "cruft" or sensitive fields need to be skipped. Click ''Pick fields…'', tick the ''All'' checkbox at the top to select every leaf, untick the fields you don't want, ''Apply''. Try it on the demo wiki's [[Example Moodle Gradebook]] — paste [[Example Moodle Gradebook Data]] as the source, open the editor, click the ''All'' checkbox, then untick `internal_id`, `system_token`, `audit_trail`, and `picture`. ''The All checkbox.'' Above the leaf list, an ''All'' checkbox is tri-state: //unchecked// when nothing's ticked, //checked// when every leaf is ticked, //indeterminate// when some are. Clicking it toggles between full and empty selection. Customized bindings are untouched — All only affects pure pass-throughs. ''How recognition works.'' When the picker opens, it walks your existing custom-fields and pre-ticks every binding whose value is exactly `{{}}` and whose name is a plausible flattening of `` (last segment, slugified; or the last two segments joined; or the full path joined). Bindings with transforms or extra text are //customized//, not pass-throughs — they don't appear in the picker, and unticking does not affect them. ''Field-name flattening.'' A path's proposed field name is its last segment, slugified. If that's already taken — by an existing binding or another tick — the picker walks back one segment and joins with `-`. So `author.name` becomes `name`, but if `name` is taken, `author-name`. Names are editable inline before Apply. ''What the picker does not cover.'' Leaves whose path traverses an array (e.g. `enrolledcourses[*].name`) aren't tickable — the engine rejects `[*]` inside binding tokens. Use the regular Browse modal to bind to a specific element (`enrolledcourses[0].name`). And the picker only adds rows to `custom-fields`; tw-fields (title, tags, …) are left alone, even when a tw-fields binding is itself a pass-through. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/records-path":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/records-path","caption":"Records path","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A single input above the field tables, with a Browse… button beside it. Browse opens the Path modal in //records-pick// mode: it shows the parsed JSON as a clickable tree, and clicking any record (an object inside an array, or the array itself) emits a path with the last `[N]` rewritten to `[*]`. Edit the result if you want more `[*]`s in there. If you change the records path on an existing profile and any current binding uses an ancestor reference, a yellow banner appears flagging the risk; ''Keep'' confirms or ''Revert'' restores. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/sample-pane":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/sample-pane","caption":"The Sample JSON pane","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The Sample JSON textarea is //shared// with the Console's Source JSON box — they point at the same state tiddler. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor","caption":"The profile editor","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/sample-pane $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/records-path $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/fields-tables $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/browse-modal $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/live-save $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/pass-through","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Open the editor by: * Clicking ''New…'' next to the Console's profile dropdown (creates an empty profile and opens it). * Clicking ''Edit'' next to the profile dropdown when a profile is selected. * Clicking the ''Edit in form'' button atop any profile tiddler's view (provided by the plugin's ViewTemplate). !!! The fastest way to see what the tool does: # Click <$button class="tc-btn-invisible" tooltip="Open the Console"><$action-navigate $to="$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/Console"/>{{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/icon}} — or the matching icon in the page-controls toolbar (top-right) — to open the Console. # Pick ''Example Reading List'' from the //Profile// dropdown. # Open the ''Example Reading List Data'' tiddler from the sidebar, click its ''Copy text'' button, and paste into the //Source JSON// box of the Console. # Click ''Convert''. Eight tiddlers appear under //Staging//, none in conflict. # Click ''Apply''. Eight book tiddlers are written to the wiki. An ''Imported this session'' list at the bottom of the Console lets you click through them. Try modifying the profile next — click ''Edit'' beside the dropdown. The profile editor opens with the profile's records path, TiddlyWiki fields, and custom fields shown as editable rows. Change something, save (it's automatic), and re-run the conversion to see the effect. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator/good-importers":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator/good-importers","caption":"What makes a good importer","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"An importer is used by someone who will not read this guide. What makes one good is that they never need to. * ''Name it for the data, not the tool.'' //Invoice Importer//, //Import Invoices//, //Stage invoices//. The words "JSON" and "convert" mean nothing to the recipient; "invoices" means everything. * ''One profile per importer.'' A wiki that takes invoices and receipts installs two importers. Each keeps its own working data, its own page, its own sample, and can be regenerated on its own. * ''Ship a sample.'' ''Try it with the sample'' lets the recipient watch the whole thing work before trusting it with real data, and the recorded shape is what lets the panel say "this doesn't look like what I expect" instead of staging nothing. Use a small, real-looking export -- three records, not three hundred. * ''Write the introduction for a stranger.'' Where does this JSON come from, how do they get it, what comes out. Two sentences. //Paste the export from the invoice scanner below, or drop the file on the box. Each invoice becomes a tiddler titled by its invoice number.// * ''Choose the collision default deliberately.'' //skip// is safe for a re-import that must not clobber edits; //overwrite// suits a feed that is the source of truth. The recipient can still change it per tiddler. * ''Keep the studio URL true.'' It is where every "ask whoever made this" message points. If you generate from a copy of the studio on your own machine, the generator falls back to the public studio's address; set it to wherever you will actually be reachable. * ''Test in an empty wiki once.'' Download the combined file, drag it into a fresh `empty.html`, reload, and run the sample. That is the recipient's first five minutes; if anything surprises you there, it will surprise them more. * ''Bump, don't rename.'' When the profile changes, regenerate under the same publisher and slug with a higher version. The recipient drags in the new file and TiddlyWiki replaces the old one. A new slug would install a second importer beside the first. * ''Mind JavaScript.'' A pack carries JavaScript only if the profile uses a custom JavaScript transform. The generator says so. Prefer a wikitext transform when one will do, and hand a JavaScript-carrying pack only to people who already trust you. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator","caption":"Generating an importer","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator/good-importers","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Once a profile works against your data, you can bake it into an //importer//: a small plugin that somebody else installs and uses without ever seeing the profile, the Console or the editor. They get a page named for their data — listed under ''More › Importers'' in the sidebar and linked from the plugin's readme — with a box to paste into, ''Convert'' and ''Apply''. !!! Making one # In the Console, select the profile and click ''Generate importer…'' (the same button sits on the profile tiddler itself). The generator opens with sensible defaults filled in. # Check the ''publisher'' and ''slug''. Together they make the plugin's title, `$:/plugins//`, and the slug also names the importer's working data, so two importers in one wiki must differ. # Give it a ''name'', a ''caption'' the recipient will click, and an ''introduction'' that says where the JSON comes from and what comes out. Label the ''Convert'' button for the data: //Stage invoices// beats //Convert//. # Pick ''sample data'' if you have some. It ships in the pack behind a ''Try it with the sample'' button, and its shape is recorded so the panel can tell the recipient when their JSON does not look like what the profile expects. # Click ''Generate''. The pack is installed in this wiki at once, so you can open the new importer page exactly as the recipient will see it. Hand it over by dragging the plugin tiddler onto their wiki, or download it: * ''Download pack'' — for a wiki that already has the JSON Convert runtime. * ''Download pack + runtime'' — one file for a wiki with nothing installed. A wiki that already has the same or a newer runtime keeps its own and takes just the pack. !!! What goes in the pack * A copy of the profile, with `"format": 1` stamped in, under the pack's own title so an ordinary tiddler can never shadow it by accident. * Every custom transform the profile references, copied with its name. A transform that does not exist is a generation error, not a surprise for the recipient. Transforms that ship with the runtime are not copied. * The sample and its shape fingerprint, if you chose one. * A short readme, shown in the recipient's plugin list: what the importer does, a link to its page, the fields it expects, and where it came from. * The panel tiddler: the caption, the labels, the collision default, the lowest runtime version the pack needs, and this studio's URL, so every "ask whoever made this" message in the panel points back here. See [[Importer pack fields|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/pack-fields]] for the exact fields. !!! Regenerating The [[Studio|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/Studio]] page lists every importer made here, says when its profile has been edited since, and has a ''Regenerate…'' button that opens the generator with all of that importer's settings and the version bumped. A recipient who drags in the new file gets the newer pack and TiddlyWiki discards the old one. If you have lost the original profile, dragging a pack into this wiki puts its profile in the Console's dropdown, where you can edit it and generate afresh; ''Regenerate…'' then uses the copy inside the pack. !!! JavaScript A pack carries JavaScript only when it includes a JavaScript transform. The generator says so when it does. The recipient should take such a pack only from someone they trust — which, for a hand-delivered importer, they already do. !!! [[12.1 What makes a good importer|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator/good-importers]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator/good-importers}} "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/conventions":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/conventions","caption":"The conventions","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Keep this checklist in mind for hand-written profiles: * The tiddler's `type` must be `application/json`. * Its `tags` must include `$:/tags/json-convert/profile`. * The body must be valid JSON (no trailing commas, double-quoted strings). * `records` must be a single template token. * `tw-fields.title` is required. * All transform names must be registered (built-ins or any tiddler tagged `$:/tags/json-convert/transform`). "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/minimum":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/minimum","caption":"The minimum","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"``` title: My Profile type: application/json tags: $:/tags/json-convert/profile { "records": "{{items[*]}}", "tw-fields": { "title": "{{name}}" } } ``` That's a complete, runnable profile. Pick it in the Console; paste a JSON document with a top-level `items` array of objects each having a `name` field; click Convert. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/validate":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/validate","caption":"Validate by opening in the editor","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"If you're not sure your hand-written profile is valid, open it in the editor. The validation banner at the top will be either green (''Profile valid'') or red with a click-to-expand list of every problem — each entry focuses the offending row when clicked. Fix until green; close the editor; the live-save will have re-written the JSON to its canonical form. Hand-edited and editor-saved profiles are interchangeable; the editor reads and writes the same shape. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor","caption":"Writing a profile without the editor","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/minimum $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/conventions $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/validate","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The editor is convenient but never required. A profile is just JSON in a tiddler. You can write one by hand and never touch the editor. !!! [[9.1 The minimum|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/minimum]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/minimum}} !!! [[9.2 The conventions|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/conventions]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/conventions}} !!! [[9.3 Validate by opening in the editor|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/validate]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/no-editor/validate}} "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/ancestors":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/ancestors","caption":"Ancestor scopes — `..`","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"When the records path crosses multiple `[*]`s, each `[*]` opens a new scope. Bindings normally resolve against the innermost scope (the current record), but leading `..` segments step back up: * `{{field}}` — the current record (the item) * `{{../field}}` — the parent scope (the subgroup) * `{{../../field}}` — the grandparent (the group) * `{{../../../field}}` — the document root The number of `..`s a binding may use is bounded by the //records-path depth// — the count of `[*]`s. Exceeding it is a validation error (`binding-parent-too-deep`). A records path with no `[*]` still exposes one ancestor (the document root) for backward compatibility. `..` is not allowed in the `records` token itself — iteration always starts from the document root. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/basics":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/basics","caption":"The basics","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Paths read left to right. `meta.course` resolves `meta` against the root, then `course` against the result. `questions[2].name` indexes into an array then reads a property. Reserved characters (`.`, `[`, `]`, `/`) can't appear in keys. If any step along the way is missing or has the wrong type, the path resolves to `undefined`, which becomes the empty string in a binding plus a ''path-missing'' warning. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/iteration":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/iteration","caption":"`[*]` — iteration","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"`[*]` means "every element." It's valid only inside the `records` token. A binding that contained `[*]` would produce an array, not a string, which doesn't make sense for a single tiddler field — the validator rejects it (`binding-token-star`). "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/nested":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/nested","caption":"Nested iteration","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A `records` path can chain multiple `[*]`s to iterate through nested arrays: ``` "records": "{{groups[*].subgroups[*].items[*]}}" ``` This produces one tiddler //per leaf item// — every item across every subgroup across every group. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths","caption":"Path expressions","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/basics $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/iteration $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/nested $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/ancestors","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Paths address values inside the parsed JSON. |!Form |!Meaning |!Where allowed | |`key` |object property access |anywhere | |`key.subkey` |chained property |anywhere | |`key[0]` |concrete array index |anywhere | |`key[*]` |iterate every array element |only in `records` | |`a.b[0].c.d` |mixed access |anywhere | |`a[*].b[*].c` |nested iteration |only in `records` | |`..` |step up one ancestor scope |only in binding tokens (§5.4) | !!! [[5.1 The basics|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/basics]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/basics}} !!! [[5.2 `[*]` — iteration|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/iteration]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/iteration}} !!! [[5.3 Nested iteration|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/nested]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/nested}} !!! [[5.4 Ancestor scopes — `..`|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/ancestors]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths/ancestors}} "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/bindings":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/bindings","caption":"Bindings","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A //binding// is a //template string//. Each `{{...}}` in it is a //token// that resolves a path against the current record and substitutes the result. Anything outside `{{...}}` is literal text: ``` "{{course}}/{{name}}-{{id}}" ← three tokens, two literal "/" and "-" separators "text/vnd.tiddlywiki" ← no tokens, plain literal "{{message|html-to-wikitext}}" ← one token, piped through a transform ``` See [[Section 6|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/tokens]] for the full token grammar. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/fields":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/fields","caption":"tw-fields and custom-fields","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Both are maps from //field name// to //binding//. The two keys are functionally identical — the engine treats them the same — but the editor presents them as separate tables and seeds `tw-fields` with a curated set of common standard fields (`title`, `tags`, `caption`, `text`). `tw-fields` is for known TiddlyWiki standard fields; `custom-fields` is for everything else. A field name appearing in both is rejected (`field-redefined`). `title` is required in `tw-fields`. Everything else is optional. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/normalize":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/normalize","caption":"normalize","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Optional. A list of steps that reshape the source document before the records path is resolved. Everything downstream — bindings, the shape trees, the field picker — sees the reshaped document. One step exists, `pivot`. It turns an array of entry-objects into the object those entries describe, which is what you need when a source reports each field as `{"key": "date", "value": "9/16/26", "type": "string"}` rather than as `"date": "9/16/26"`: ``` "normalize": [{"pivot": {}}] ``` With no options, pivot rewrites every array in the document whose elements all carry both a `key` and a `value` property; anything else is left alone. Values are copied across unchanged, so numbers stay numbers and transforms still apply. Duplicate keys within one group resolve last-wins, with a warning, and a step that matches nothing raises `normalize-no-effect`. |!Option |!Default |!Meaning | |`key` |`"key"` |Property holding the field name | |`value` |`"value"` |Property holding the field value | |`at` |whole document |Path limiting the rewrite (`[*]` allowed, `..` not) | The Console's ''Flatten key/value pair arrays'' checkbox writes and removes the default step for you, and the profile editor has the same checkbox above the records path. Hand-written options survive editing either way. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/records":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/records","caption":"records","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A single template token whose path resolves to the array of records. Each element of that array becomes one tiddler. See [[Section 5|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/paths]] for the path syntax. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/stamp":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/stamp","caption":"`stamp`","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Optional. The list of fields ''Apply'' fills in from the moment of import when the profile does not bind them: any of `created`, `modified`, `creator`, `modifier`. ``` "stamp": ["created", "modified"] ← the default when the key is absent "stamp": [] ← stamp nothing "stamp": ["modified", "modifier"] ← modifier takes $:/status/UserName ``` Rules: * A field the profile binds is never stamped over. * Overwriting an existing tiddler never changes its `created` or `creator` by stamping; only a bound value does. `modified` and `modifier` are stamped fresh. * A renamed or added tiddler is new, so its creation fields are fresh. * Any other name is a `bad-stamp` error. The editor shows the four as checkboxes under the records path and writes the key only when the choice differs from the default. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles","caption":"Profiles — the data model","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/records $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/fields $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/bindings $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/normalize $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/stamp","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A profile is a tiddler whose: * ''title'' — anything human-readable * ''type'' — `application/json` * ''tags'' — include `$:/tags/json-convert/profile` * ''text'' — JSON conforming to the schema below For a friendlier walkthrough with screenshots, see <>. ``` { "records": "{{...}}", ← required, path to the records array "normalize": [ ... steps ... ], ← optional, reshapes the source first "stamp": [ ... fields ... ], ← optional, what Apply fills in (default created, modified) "tw-fields": { ... bindings ... }, ← required, must include "title" "custom-fields": { ... bindings ... } ← optional } ``` !!!
