[[4.5 `stamp`|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/stamp]] {{$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/profiles/stamp}} "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/iterating":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/iterating","caption":"Iterating on a profile","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Typical edit/run cycle: # Paste source once into the Console. # Convert with the current profile. # Note errors/warnings; if a binding misbehaves, click ''Edit'' to open the editor (paste survives — Source JSON is shared). # Adjust the binding; the live save persists immediately. # Switch back to the Console; ''Convert'' again — the now-updated profile is re-read. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/lookup-at-import":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/lookup-at-import","caption":"Looking up a related tiddler at import","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"A wikitext transform runs with the whole wiki in scope, so a binding can set a field by looking something up rather than copying it. The motivating case: index cards carry a student's initials, and a roster tiddler per student carries those initials in an `init` field under an anonymous title. The import should record the roster title, not the initials. ``` title: Student ID name: student-id tags: $:/tags/json-convert/transform type: text/vnd.tiddlywiki <$text text={{{ [listed[init]removeprefix[—]] }}}/> ``` ``` "custom-fields": { "initials": "{{initials_or_name}}", "student": "{{initials_or_name|student-id}}" } ``` Initials the roster does not know come out as an empty `student` field; the readable initials stay in their own field for checking afterwards. ''Keying on more than one field.'' Every transform also receives the whole record — as the `record` variable in wikitext, holding the record as JSON text — so a lookup can qualify by a second field. Bind `{{@record|student-id}}` and read what you need inside: ``` <$text text={{{ [jsonget[initials]] :filter[jsonget[class]match[101]] +[listed[init]removeprefix[—]] }}}/> ``` The same shape serves a citation string looked up against a bibliography, or any locally important relational key. Two cautions: the lookup target must exist in the wiki the import runs in, which for an importer pack means the recipient's wiki; and a lookup that finds nothing yields '', so pair it with `default[…]` if a placeholder is better than a blank. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/many-fields":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/many-fields","caption":"Importing many fields at once","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Source JSON has thirty fields and you want twenty-eight of them? Don't enumerate them by hand. Open the editor, click ''Pick fields…'' next to the Custom Fields header, untick the two you don't want, ''Apply''. See [[Section 7.6|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/editor/pass-through]] for the picker's full behavior. The picker writes ordinary `"": "{{}}"` bindings — same shape as if you'd typed them. Reopening the picker re-recognizes them, so adding more fields later (or removing some of what you picked) is just another round-trip. Customize a binding through the row UI (`{{name|to-upper-case}}`) and the picker treats it as out of scope; an accidental untick can't destroy customizations. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/messy-input":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/messy-input","caption":"Handling messy input","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"* If your source has a BOM or noise around the JSON, the parser will strip it and emit a ''parse-recovered'' warning — no profile changes needed. * If a field is sometimes missing from a record, the binding produces empty and emits a ''path-missing'' warning per record. Decide whether that's acceptable; if not, source-side cleanup is usually easier than profile-side defensiveness. * For mixed types (a field that's a number in some records, a string in others), the engine's automatic stringification handles both. If you want consistent capitalization or formatting, pipe through a transform. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/multiple-inputs":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/multiple-inputs","caption":"One profile, multiple inputs","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Same schema, different sources. The ''Example Moodle Forum'' profile works on both ''Example Moodle Forum Data'' and the noisy ''Example Moodle Forum Data (with junk)'' fixture — the tolerant parser handles the extra wrapping in the latter. For your own: * Hand-write a profile that uses only the fields the inputs have in common. * Run multiple Converts against it with different paste-ins. Each Convert is independent; previous Applies don't interfere unless titles collide. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/multiple-profiles":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/multiple-profiles","caption":"One input, multiple profiles","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Same data, different output goals. This wiki's ''Example Music Library'' and ''Example Music Library — by Album'' profiles both read the same data tiddler but produce per-track or per-album tiddlers respectively. To wire your own: * Author profile A with `records: "{{[*].albums[*].tracks[*]}}"` and per-track fields. * Author profile B with `records: "{{[*].albums[*]}}"` and per-album fields, using `{{../artist-name}}` to reach into the parent scope. Pick one in the Console, convert, apply. Switch profiles, re-paste (or reuse the same paste — Source JSON is sticky), re-convert. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/nested-records":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/nested-records","caption":"Records nested 2-3 levels deep","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Use multiple `[*]`s in the records path; use `..` in bindings to reach the ancestors. See the ''Example Trip Itinerary'' profile, which exercises 3-deep nesting (trip → days → activities) with `../date` and `../../trip-name`. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/number-records":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/number-records","caption":"Numbering the records","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"`@counter` is the record's position in the run, counting from 1 like the `$list` widget's counter. Padded, it sorts: ``` "tw-fields": { "title": "Card {{@counter|zero-pad[3]}}" } ``` gives `Card 001`, `Card 002`, … When the data has its own identifier, pad that instead — `{{unique_id|zero-pad[4]}}` — and keep `@counter` for a batch position or a tie-breaker: ``` "custom-fields": { "batch-order": "{{@counter}}", "id": "{{unique_id|zero-pad[4]}}" } ``` The counter restarts at 1 on every ''Convert'', so it is a position within one import, not an identity across imports. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/recover-apply":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/recover-apply","caption":"Recovering from a bad Apply","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The ''Imported this session'' list at the bottom of the Console is your undo log. Click a title to navigate to it; delete or edit as needed. The list is per-session — on reload it's empty. For longer-term tracking, consider tagging imported tiddlers (via a binding in the profile, e.g. `"tags": "Imported {{...}}"`) so you can filter for them later. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/stamp-import-time":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/stamp-import-time","caption":"Stamping the import time","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Imported tiddlers get `created` and `modified` at ''Apply'', set to the moment of import, unless the profile binds those fields itself — so they appear under Recent, and a re-import that overwrites keeps the original `created`. Nothing to write for the common case. To turn that off, or to add the rarely wanted `creator` and `modifier`, use the `stamp` key (or the checkboxes under the editor's records path): ``` "stamp": [] ← nothing stamped "stamp": ["created", "modified", "creator"] ← creator too ``` To put the import time in a field of your own, bind the `@now` context path. It is already in TiddlyWiki's date format: ``` "custom-fields": { "imported-at": "{{@now}}" } ``` And when the data carries its own dates, bind them — a bound field always wins over a stamp: ``` "tw-fields": { "created": "{{created_at|iso-to-date}}", "modified": "{{updated_at|iso-to-date}}" } ``` "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/uninstall-cleanup":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/uninstall-cleanup","caption":"Cleaning up before uninstall","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"TiddlyWiki has no plugin-uninstall hook, so state tiddlers under `$:/state/json-convert/...` persist after the plugins are removed. These are the Console's pasted source and chosen profile, and the editor's working state — small and inert, but if you want a clean uninstall: ``` <$button> Clean up json-convert state <$list filter="[prefix[$:/state/json-convert/]]" variable="t"> <$action-deletetiddler $tiddler=<>/> ``` Paste that into a new tiddler, click the button, then uninstall the plugins — the Studio first, then the runtime. Everything a ''Convert'' produces (staged tiddlers, decisions, results, the session log) lives under `$:/temp/...`, which is session-only and needs no cleanup. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes","caption":"Recipes","list":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/multiple-profiles $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/multiple-inputs $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/nested-records $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/messy-input $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/iterating $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/many-fields $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/recover-apply $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/uninstall-cleanup $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/stamp-import-time $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/number-records $:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/recipes/lookup-at-import","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"!!! carries `detail` (which step failed and what was there) and `document` | |`missing-title-binding` |`tw-fields` is missing, isn't an object, or doesn't contain a `title` key | |`tw-fields-not-object` |`tw-fields` exists but isn't an object | |`custom-fields-not-object` |`custom-fields` exists but isn't an object | |`field-redefined` |a `custom-fields` key is also in `tw-fields` | |`binding-bad-shape` |a binding is not a string | |`binding-bad-token` |a `{{...}}` token has invalid path / empty path / empty transform / unterminated braces | |`binding-token-star` |a binding token uses `[*]` (allowed only in `records`) | |`binding-parent-too-deep` |a binding's `..` count exceeds the records-path depth | |`unknown-transform` |a transform name isn't registered | |`normalize-not-array` |`normalize` exists but isn't an array | |`unknown-normalize-step` |a `normalize` step isn't a single recognized operation | |`normalize-bad-step` |a `pivot` step has an unknown option, a non-string option, or a bad `at` path | |`bad-stamp` |`stamp` is not a list, or names a field other than `created`, `modified`, `creator`, `modifier` | ''Run-time errors'' (per record; the rest of the conversion continues): |!Code |!Cause | |`parse-failed` |source JSON couldn't be parsed even after recovery; carries `line`, `column` and `excerpt` where the host engine reports them | |`missing-title` |a record's `title` binding evaluated to an empty string; carries `binding`, `keys` (the record's keys) and `excerpt` | |`duplicate-title` |a record's title collides with one already produced this batch | ''Warnings'': |!Code |!Cause | |`parse-recovered` |source JSON parsed only after stripping BOM/junk | |`records-empty` |`records` matched no records (zero tiddlers produced); carries `detail` (the first step that matched nothing) and `document` | |`path-missing` |a binding token's path resolved to `undefined` | |`normalize-no-effect` |a `pivot` step matched no key/value pair arrays | |`normalize-duplicate-key` |a `pivot` step found the same key twice in one group; last wins | "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/pack-fields":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/pack-fields","caption":"Importer pack fields","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"An //importer pack// is a plugin that carries one profile and a panel tiddler. The panel tiddler's fields configure the runtime's consumer panel (`$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert/ui/consumer-panel`), which the panel tiddler transcludes with `pack=` set to its own title. The demo wiki ships one, `$:/plugins/crosseye/reading-list-importer`, hand-built as the reference for what the [[generator|$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/generator]] emits. |!Field |!Required |!Purpose | |`slug` |yes |Namespace key; working data lives under `$:/temp/json-convert//` | |`profile` |yes |Title of the profile tiddler (inside the pack) | |`caption` |yes |The page's name, e.g. //Import Invoices//; the runtime's ''More › Importers'' tab lists it | |`description` |no |Wikitext shown at the top of the panel | |`sample` |no |Title of a JSON tiddler offered by ''Try it with the sample'' | |`shape` |no |Title of the sample's shape fingerprint; the panel compares pasted JSON against it | |`convert-label` |no |Label for the Convert button (default ''Convert'') | |`apply-label` |no |Label for the Apply button (default ''Apply'') | |`collisions` |no |Default decision for existing titles: `skip` (default) or `overwrite` | |`runtime-min` |no |Lowest runtime version the pack needs; the panel warns below it | |`studio-url` |no |Where the pack was made; every "ask whoever made this" message links here | |`author` |no |Who made it; the same messages name them | Alongside the panel tiddler the pack holds `/readme` (what the importer does, a link to its page, the fields it expects), `/profile`, optional `/sample` and `/shape` (the sample's record shape, as `engine/shape.js` merges it, with the records path and count), and one `/transforms/` per custom transform the profile references. The plugin tiddler itself carries `json-convert-pack: `, which is how the runtime's ''More › Importers'' tab and the studio hub find installed packs. The panel is not tagged into the sidebar: an importer is an occasional task, and the story river has room for the pasted JSON and the staged tiddlers. The profile carries `"format": 1` so a future runtime that no longer reads that format can say so. The panel tiddler's text is a small shim: if the runtime's consumer panel exists it transcludes it, otherwise it shows a sentence saying which plugin to install and where to get it. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/path-grammar":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/path-grammar","caption":"Path expression grammar","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"``` path := "@" context-name ( "." … )? | segment ( separator segment )* segment := key | "[" ( index | "*" ) "]" | "[" quoted "]" key := [^.[\]/]+ (one or more non-reserved chars) quoted := '"' ( [^"\\] | '\\"' | '\\\\' )* '"' (any key at all, escaped) index := [0-9]+ separator:= "." | (no separator before "[") prefix := ( ".." "/" )* (only in binding tokens) ``` ''Context paths.'' A first segment `@now`, `@counter` or `@record` names something about the import rather than the data; see the token grammar. A data key that starts with `@` is reached through a quoted segment. ''Quoted segments.'' A key the bare syntax cannot express — one containing `.`, `[`, `]` or `/`, an empty one, or one starting with `@` (reserved for context paths) — is written in double quotes inside brackets, with no dot before it: `["first.last"].x`, `data["odd key"][*]`, `["@id"]`. Inside the quotes `\"` and `\\` are the only escapes. The pickers emit this form automatically for such keys. "},"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/schema":{"title":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference/schema","caption":"Profile JSON schema","tags":"$:/plugins/crosseye/json-convert-studio/usage/reference","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"``` { "format": 1, ← optional, profile format version (absent means 1) "records": string, ← required, a single template token "normalize": [ step, … ], ← optional, reshapes the source first "stamp": [ field, … ], ← optional, fields Apply fills in (default ["created", "modified"]) "tw-fields": { name: binding, … }, ← required, must include "title" "custom-fields": { name: binding, … } ← optional } binding := string (a template string; items under `$:/temp/...` are session-only. The Console keeps only its //inputs// — the pasted source and the chosen profile — in `$:/state`, so the bench survives a reload; everything a ''Convert'' produces lives in `$:/temp` and never reaches disk. Parameters are positional and always strings; a transform that wants a number parses it. A built-in given the wrong parameters leaves the value alone. * Transforms chain left to right: `{{x|default[none]|prefix[<]|suffix[>]}}`. * `@now` is the import time as a TiddlyWiki date; `@counter` the record's position counting from 1; `@record` the record as JSON text, or a path into it. A context path stands alone: `../@now` and `@now.x` are errors. * A missing path still runs its transforms, with an undefined value, so `default[…]` can supply one; the `path-missing` warning is emitted regardless. binding : '' wiki.addTiddler({ title: `${prefix}${name}`, value }) } const orderedNames = (group, profileMap) => { const profileKeys = Object.keys(profileMap) if (group !== 'tw-fields') return profileKeys const seedSet = new Set(TW_FIELD_SEED) const extras = profileKeys.filter((k) => !seedSet.has(k)) return [...TW_FIELD_SEED, ...extras] } const writeFieldGroup = (wiki, draftBase, group, profileMap) => { const prefix = `${draftBase}${group}/` const obj = isPlainObject(profileMap) ?
